sections.title: What this module covers
sections.body: Ruby metaprogramming is the capability that makes Rails associations, validations, and callbacks possible — and it is a reliable topic in senior Ruby interviews. This page covers the techniques interviewers probe: method_missing and why respond_to_missing? must always accompany it; define_method for generating methods dynamically at class load time; send vs public_send and the security difference; class_eval and instance_eval for executing code in a different binding; and the class macro pattern that powers has_many, validates, and before_action. The gotchas are equally important: method_missing is slow (it fires after the full method lookup fails), hard to debug, and easy to misuse. Every answer includes when to reach for each technique and when to prefer a simpler alternative.

sections.title: Key topics and depth markers
sections.body: Topics: method-missing, define-method, send-eval, dsl-patterns. Each topic has dedicated Q&A covering the concept, the comparison, the internal mechanics, and the scenario-based questions interviewers use to test production understanding.

sections.title: How interviewers probe this module
sections.body: Interviewers at Rails-focused companies probe these topics by opening with a definition question, then immediately following up with when would you use X vs Y? and what are the gotchas?. The depth marker is always the trade-off and the failure mode — not just the API surface.
